fit: longitudinal Parkinson hallucination scale and probable REM sleep behavior symptoms
assessment: The reported early probable REM sleep behavior disorder group had a higher prevalence and greater later severity of hallucinations on clinical assessment. The report compares phenotype and severity over disease-time intervals. It does not count visual-only episodes after a food exposure.

fit: binary antemortem hallucination phenotype and postmortem tissue
assessment: The original labels hallucination presence or absence from antemortem clinical notes and examines methylation networks in postmortem Parkinson brain tissue. It relates biology to recorded symptom occurrence without dried fig exposure or counts of recurrent visual episodes.

fit: observational dopaminergic infusion and adverse-event reports
assessment: ELEGANCE interim safety analysis covers 167 treated Parkinson patients. The narrative counts seven patients with any hallucination report and notes resolution in six. The adverse-event table separately codes visual hallucination and its serious subset. These are drug-treatment reports, not episode rates following dried fig.

fit: psychosis scales across Parkinson and atypical diagnosis groups
assessment: The Parkinson comparison group contributes MDS-UPDRS psychosis scores. The Cambridge Behavioural Inventory in other diagnostic groups separately asks about visual and auditory hallucinations and beliefs. Scale and group differences provide no food-attributed visual episode comparison.

fit: cerebral microbleeds and presence of visual hallucinations
assessment: Among 929 mixed Lewy body and Parkinson cognitive syndrome patients, the crude odds ratio linking microbleeds with visual hallucination presence was 1.264 with a confidence interval crossing one. The fully adjusted OR was 1.597 with 95% CI 1.014–2.517. This is diagnostic-cohort symptom presence, with no dietary exposure or recurrence measure.

fit: genetic disease and psychiatric presentation in a case series
assessment: Three of 958 patients in a psychiatry-based dementia cohort had pathological NOTCH2NLC expansions. Their case histories and diagnostic work-up describe different disorders and do not measure a response to dried fig consumption.

fit: sleep-transition hallucinations and other psychiatric symptoms in narcolepsy
assessment: The literature review distinguishes sleep-transition hallucinations and psychiatric comorbidities in narcolepsy cohorts. It describes a separate sleep disorder and does not measure Parkinson visual episode frequency after fig consumption.

fit: separate visual, medication and nutritional cases in the general medicine congress
assessment: The complete meeting publication includes separate cases of recurrent Charles Bonnet phenomena, severe malnutrition after sleeve gastrectomy, medication-associated perceptual symptoms and vision loss in a person with Parkinson. The original members do not connect measured dried fig intake to Parkinson visual episode frequency.

fit: stimulation-elicited visual sensations in an epilepsy cohort
assessment: The original study records intracranial EEG and elicited visual sensations in 69 people with medically refractory epilepsy selected for reporting an induced percept. The experimental comparison is stimulation-related physiology. It does not measure clinical Parkinson visual episodes or food exposure.

fit: validation of Parkinson perceptual and behavioral rating items
assessment: The Canadian study assesses the Mild Behavioral Impairment Checklist in Parkinson and compares model structures and agreement with other clinical ratings. Visual and auditory items are separable. The authors report instability in the psychosis domain, and the design does not test any food.

fit: Parkinson reading and contrast vision tested during drug and stimulation states
assessment: The original uses within-person levodopa or stimulation comparisons for reading speed and color contrast acuity. Immediate comparisons were generally inconclusive, with exploratory changes in selected conditions after surgery. The visual tasks do not count spontaneous hallucinations after eating.

fit: clinical scale scope and psychosis outcome distinctions
assessment: The Movement Disorder Society scoping review surveys outcome assessment instruments across 19 Parkinson constructs and 504 included studies. It discusses measurement and validation context, with no primary exposure or food-attributed episode-frequency measurement.

fit: Parkinson variant groups and clinical nonmotor phenotype
assessment: The original genotypes 3,058 Malaysian Parkinson participants, with detailed phenotyping in 185. The reported nonmotor comparison shows no group differences for visual hallucinations. This is a genetic subgroup comparison, with no tested dried fig consumption or timed clinical episode rates.

fit: sex and gender in phenotypes across Lewy body disorders
assessment: The narrative review synthesizes published differences in diagnosis, symptom profiles, progression and treatment in Lewy body disorders. Reported visual symptom differences are secondary clinical context without ingredient intake or measured food-timed recurrence.

fit: documented ICU episode timing and modality outside Parkinson food exposure
assessment: In 7,525 critically ill adults, clinical note screening identified 625 with hallucinations. Among those 625, 281 had more than one documented episode of any modality. Median time until the first episode resolved was 15 hours. Medication associations use a nested cohort. The design does not measure dried figs, Parkinson-specific episodes or a food-timed effect.
